ns2:section.sectionText: This course focuses on research examining the experiences of Black families in K-12 schools. Historical, social, economic, and contextual factors that influence these experiences will be considered. Black Families in schools will explore topics such as the history of Black schools, racial identity development, racial socialization, parent engagement in schools, parent-child relationships, critical consciousness and how these topics relate to student experiences in schools. The ultimate goal of this course is to enable you to think critically about education as a social institution and how it relates to Black family’s experiences within that space and how race and ethnicity play a role.
